Care guides

The four basics

Read the room before you place a plant

Most houseplants want bright, indirect light: close enough to a window to see the sky, but out of the harsh midday beam. A sheer curtain makes almost any sunny window work.

  • North-facing rooms suit ferns, calatheas and snake plants.
  • East and west windows are the sweet spot for most foliage.
  • South-facing sills are for cacti, succulents and citrus.

Water when the top two centimetres of soil are dry, then water thoroughly until it drains.

Our pots ship with a chunky, peat-free mix that drains quickly and holds air around the roots.

Group tropical plants together or set them on a pebble tray to raise humidity in winter.
